setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Smokestack Lightning** (2 reviews): Reviewer insists Garcia is playing here despite the text file saying he is absent; Elvin takes over for his own tune and Beat It On Down The Line; Reviewer calls this amazing and singles out Pigpen's harmonica playing [7][11]
- **Checkin' Up On My Baby** (1 review, 1 other source): The band plays straighter blues here than elsewhere, and Elvin warns them not to blow it as they rush ahead; Wayne Ceballos adds vocals here, and there is a minor, barely noticeable splice at 1:14 [1][4]
- **Beat It On Down The Line** (1 review, 1 other source): Someone botches playing on this song; Deadbase omits him from it, though he is audibly present; Wayne Ceballos adds vocals on this song, with Elvin Bishop on lead and no Garcia [1][6]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (2 reviews): Garcia arrives to save the show; around 15-20 minutes in the band breaks down into genre-defying psychedelic improvisation while Pigpen urges them to wait; Confirms Pigpen handles the vocals on this Lovelight [10][11]
- **Green, Green Grass Of Home** (1 other source): Elvin Bishop plays on this song, with Garcia apparently stepping out [2]

## Setlist highlights

- **Green, Green Grass Of Home**: rare: 8 archived performances [15]
- **Checkin' Up On My Baby**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]

## The recordings

- **gd69-06-06.sbd.jupile.9494.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 6 songs; 77 min; rated 3.68/5 by 19 [1]
- **gd1969-06-06.sbd.thecore.4281.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 3 songs; 64 min [2]

## Around the show

- Reportedly someone dosed the apple juice with LSD; Phil Lesh said he was propped against an amp, and Hunter hallucinated [5]
- Per Phil's book, apple juice caused confusion, players were out of sync, Garcia reportedly arrived late, and Phil barely made it onstage [8]
- Elvin Bishop plays guitar on every track except Lovelight, apparently using Garcia's Gibson SG and Twin Reverb amps with a similar lead style [9]
- Wayne Ceballos said he was onstage at this show; the Lost Live Dead blog covers this show and the one on the 8th [14]
- Garcia is missing for the first five songs with Elvin Bishop on lead; the crowd, Phil and Bob acknowledge his absence after Smokestack [1]
- Describes this as unlike other Dead shows because Elvin Bishop fills in for Garcia as an aggressive lead player pushing the band harder [4]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-06-06.sbd.jupile.9494.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Joe Jupille and J. Cotsman; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Notes an obvious splice around 33:25 in the Lovelight, with a tonal change in vocals and sudden long guitar sustain, undocumented in the text files [13]
- **gd1969-06-06.sbd.thecore.4281.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>MC>C>D>CD [2]. Also: This copy is not the complete show, and Lovelight has several static bursts near the 10:00 mark [2]
